question: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Hong Kong, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

notes.anthropic: The first blue-chip mega-gallery to plant a flag in Hong Kong (2011), its Pedder Building space set the template for the city's international gallery scene and still stages museum-calibre shows.
notes.openai: The Hong Kong branch of the global powerhouse, with museum-calibre exhibitions and unmatched blue-chip reach.

notes.anthropic: Anchor tenant of H Queen's since 2018, bringing Wolfgang Tillmans, Yayoi Kusama and Michaël Borremans to Asia and driving the market's centre of gravity toward Hong Kong.
notes.openai: An exceptionally influential international gallery with a strong programme of canonical and mid-career artists.

notes.anthropic: Two-floor flagship with an ambitious estates and historical programme (Louise Bourgeois, Philip Guston) plus strong Asian artist representation and education programming.
notes.openai: A major international gallery whose ambitious Hong Kong programme connects leading global and Asian artists.

notes.anthropic: In Hong Kong since 2012; a street-level space that gave the city early exposure to the YBAs and now to Tracey Emin, Antony Gormley and Asian names such as Zhou Li.
notes.openai: A longstanding Hong Kong presence presenting major international artists in institutionally scaled exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: A pioneer of the Asia market with deep Chinese contemporary ties (Zhang Xiaogang, Yoshitomo Nara) and a strong record with teamLab and light/technology art.
notes.openai: A leading global gallery with deep modern and contemporary holdings and a substantial art-fair presence.

galleries.name: Para Site
galleries.address_hint: 22/F Wing Wah Industrial Building, 677 King's Road

notes.anthropic: Hong Kong's oldest and most internationally respected independent art space (founded 1996); its exhibitions, conferences and residencies shape curatorial discourse across Asia.
notes.openai: Hong Kong's most internationally influential independent art institution, known for research-led exhibitions and regional networks.

galleries.name: Perrotin
galleries.address_hint: K11 ATELIER Victoria Dockside, 18 Salisbury Road

notes.anthropic: Opened 2012 and later moved across the harbour; a key conduit for Murakami, JR, Daniel Arsham and emerging Asian artists with strong fair presence.
notes.openai: A globally visible gallery combining major contemporary names with influential Asian and emerging practices.

notes.anthropic: Non-collecting kunsthalle inside the former Central Police Station compound; its large-scale thematic exhibitions and performance programme are the city's critical benchmark.
notes.openai: Hong Kong's principal large-scale contemporary-art centre, commissioning major exhibitions and public programmes.

notes.anthropic: Long-standing Asia presence championing Do Ho Suh, Lee Bul, Nari Ward and Tammy Nguyen; consistently strong institutional placements from Hong Kong.
notes.openai: An early international entrant to Hong Kong with a prominent roster spanning Asia, Europe and the Americas.

notes.anthropic: Formerly Edouard Malingue; the most globally visible Hong Kong-founded gallery, representing Samson Young, Ho Tzu Nyen, Wong Ping and Tromarama with a biennial-heavy roster.
notes.openai: One of Hong Kong's most critically respected galleries, with a distinctive cross-generational international programme.

galleries.name: Blindspot Gallery
galleries.address_hint: 15/F Po Chai Industrial Building, 28 Wong Chuk Hang Road

notes.anthropic: The city's leading gallery for photography and lens-based work, with a rigorous Hong Kong and Chinese roster (South Ho, Trevor Yeung, Zhang Xiao) and strong institutional traction.
notes.openai: A leading platform for contemporary photography and conceptually rigorous practices from Hong Kong and the region.

galleries.name: de Sarthe
galleries.address_hint: 20/F Global Trade Square, 21 Wong Chuk Hang Road

notes.anthropic: Family gallery that shifted from modern masters to experimental young Chinese artists; a pioneer of the Wong Chuk Hang gallery cluster.
notes.openai: An established gallery balancing postwar material with ambitious exhibitions by Chinese and international contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Empty Gallery
galleries.address_hint: 18-19/F Grand Marine Center, 3 Yue Fung Street, Tin Wan

notes.anthropic: Black-box gallery devoted to time-based, sound and moving-image practices; its research-driven programme (Takashi Makino, Tishan Hsu, Aki Onda) has outsized critical standing.
notes.openai: An internationally admired experimental gallery focused on sound, moving image, performance and difficult-to-categorize practices.

notes.anthropic: Rem Koolhaas-designed Pedder Building space since 2016, presenting European conceptual and painting positions alongside Asian debuts.
notes.openai: An influential European gallery presenting globally established artists and selective younger positions.

notes.anthropic: The region's essential research library and public programme platform; its displays, residencies and commissions underpin scholarship on Asian contemporary art.
notes.openai: A globally important research institution whose exhibitions, library and public programmes shape Asian art history.

notes.anthropic: Major Beijing-founded gallery whose Hong Kong space shows leading Chinese and Southeast Asian artists including Ai Weiwei, Wang Du and Zhao Zhao.
notes.openai: A leading Asian gallery with particular strength in Chinese contemporary art and a broad regional footprint.

notes.anthropic: Johnson Chang's gallery, founded 1983, effectively introduced Chinese contemporary art to the world through the 1993 'China's New Art, Post-1989' exhibition.
notes.openai: A foundational gallery for Chinese contemporary art whose history and scholarship remain central to the field.

notes.anthropic: Asian outpost of the Paris/Brussels gallery, showing Picasso estate material alongside contemporary painters with strong regional collector demand.
notes.openai: A major international gallery with strong postwar, contemporary and art-fair credentials.

notes.anthropic: Influential cross-cultural programme linking Chinese abstraction, design and Western artists; a fixture of Hong Kong's fair and social art scene since 2012.
notes.openai: An influential Hong Kong-founded gallery known for Chinese abstraction, design and cross-cultural contemporary programmes.

galleries.name: Axel Vervoordt Gallery
galleries.address_hint: 21/F Coda Designer Centre, 62 Wong Chuk Hang Road

notes.anthropic: Brings the Belgian dealer's Zero, Gutai and material-based sensibility to Asia; a major draw for the Wong Chuk Hang district.
notes.openai: A respected international programme joining postwar and contemporary art through material, spiritual and spatial concerns.

notes.anthropic: Early arrival (2009) in the Pedder Building; blends postwar European masters with contemporary names such as Awol Erizku and Vik Muniz.
notes.openai: A longstanding international gallery with strong postwar, modern and blue-chip contemporary programming.

galleries.name: Rossi & Rossi
galleries.address_hint: 3C Yally Industrial Building, 6 Yip Fat Street

notes.anthropic: London-founded dealer of Himalayan and Asian art turned champion of contemporary Tibetan, Mongolian and South Asian artists.
notes.openai: A pioneering regional gallery with longstanding commitments to artists from South, Southeast and East Asia.

notes.anthropic: Hong Kong-founded gallery known for ink-informed contemporary practice and paper-based work, active in fair leadership and gallery-association advocacy.
notes.openai: A prominent Hong Kong gallery representing established and emerging artists across Chinese and international contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Katie de Tilly's gallery, open since 2001, with a socially engaged programme spanning Cambodia, Vietnam and Hong Kong and a long-running Chai Wan project space history.
notes.openai: One of Hong Kong's longest-running contemporary galleries, with an important history of supporting Asian artists.

notes.anthropic: Tokyo gallery whose two-floor Hong Kong flagship anchors Gutai and postwar Japanese art in the city, alongside contemporary Asian names.
notes.openai: A prominent Japanese-founded gallery with broad East Asian reach and particular strength in postwar Japanese art.

galleries.name: Gallery Exit
galleries.address_hint: 3/F Blue Box Factory Building, 25 Hing Wo Street, Tin Wan

notes.anthropic: Consistent supporter of Hong Kong painters and conceptual artists since 2008; a reliable barometer of local emerging practice.
notes.openai: A vital incubator for Hong Kong artists, recognized for adventurous exhibitions and long-term local commitments.

notes.anthropic: Long-established Central gallery pairing European modern names with Chinese contemporary artists such as Zhou Chunya and Ju Ming.
notes.openai: A major locally rooted gallery presenting modern masters alongside established Asian and European contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Osage Gallery
galleries.address_hint: 4/F Union Hing Yip Factory Building, 20 Hing Yip Street

notes.anthropic: Large industrial-space gallery with a quasi-institutional, research-led programme on Asian contemporary art and an associated foundation.
notes.openai: An ambitious space historically associated with large-scale, critical and interdisciplinary Asian contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: One of Hong Kong's oldest galleries (1974), bridging Chinese modern ink masters and contemporary abstraction.
notes.openai: A veteran Hong Kong gallery with sustained engagement in Chinese abstraction, ink and international contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Young curatorially minded gallery co-founded by Willem Molesworth and Ysabelle Cheung; noted for experimental shows and its role in reviving discursive energy in the local scene.
notes.openai: An influential emerging gallery whose focused exhibitions foreground artists connected to Hong Kong and its diasporas.

notes.anthropic: Founded by Dominique and Arthur de Villepin; a collector-driven space with slow, single-artist exhibitions (Zao Wou-Ki, Fu Baoshi) and strong programming ambition.
notes.openai: A high-profile gallery known for scholarly, salon-like presentations of major modern and contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Fast-growing homegrown gallery with several Hong Kong locations, known for pop-inflected and emerging international artists and sell-out fair booths.
notes.openai: A fast-rising Hong Kong gallery with an international emerging-art programme and strong collector visibility.

notes.anthropic: Young gallery with an international emerging roster and strong presence at Asian fairs since 2020.
notes.openai: A closely watched young gallery supporting experimental, research-oriented and diasporic practices.

galleries.name: Videotage
galleries.address_hint: Unit 13, Cattle Depot Artist Village, 63 Ma Tau Kok Road

notes.anthropic: Artist-run collective founded 1986; the definitive Hong Kong platform for video, media and now blockchain-related art.
notes.openai: Hong Kong's foundational moving-image and media-art organization, with an important archive and experimental programme.

notes.anthropic: Since 1977 the city's central independent arts institution; the Pao Galleries and its film/media programmes have incubated generations of local artists.
notes.openai: A central nonprofit exhibition venue with decades of support for Hong Kong visual art and interdisciplinary practice.

galleries.name: 1a space
galleries.address_hint: Unit 14, Cattle Depot Artist Village, 63 Ma Tau Kok Road

notes.anthropic: Artist-run non-profit since 1998 known for experimental, locally rooted and socially critical exhibitions at the Cattle Depot.
notes.openai: A longstanding independent organization supporting emerging artists, curators and experimental exhibition models.

notes.anthropic: Non-collecting gallery in a landmark Tadao Ando-adjacent heritage site, presenting scholarly exhibitions of Asian modern and contemporary art.
notes.openai: A respected cultural institution presenting substantial exhibitions and public discussions connecting Asia and the world.

notes.anthropic: Hollywood Road mainstay since 2008 showing Chinese and Hong Kong mid-career artists with a strong photography and painting mix.
notes.openai: An established local gallery presenting accessible but serious programmes across painting, sculpture and mixed media.

notes.anthropic: Government-run heritage art space with a community and experimental focus; a key incubator for young Hong Kong artists and public-art projects.
notes.openai: A government-run contemporary-art space known for public commissions, experimental installations and community engagement.

notes.anthropic: Soho fixture since 2000 supporting Hong Kong and Southeast Asian emerging artists through residencies and long-term relationships.
notes.openai: A longstanding independent gallery recognized for sustained support of Hong Kong and regional artists.

notes.anthropic: Founded by Henry Au-yeung, the most consistent advocate for Hong Kong-born artists and local art history over more than two decades.
notes.openai: A key advocate for Hong Kong artists since the early 2000s, with notable strength in ink and local art history.

galleries.name: K11 Art Foundation
galleries.address_hint: chi K11 art space, Victoria Dockside, 18 Salisbury Road

notes.anthropic: Adrian Cheng's foundation and its public art spaces have funded major museum collaborations and given many Chinese artists their first large platforms.
notes.openai: A large public exhibition venue supported by K11 Art Foundation, regularly hosting international contemporary projects.

notes.anthropic: Hong Kong-founded gallery promoting 'Eastern Origin' contemporary Chinese art, with a London branch and steady fair presence.
notes.openai: A Hong Kong-founded gallery specializing in Chinese contemporary art, particularly abstraction and new ink.

notes.anthropic: Focused on Nordic and Asian craft-based contemporary art, with a strong ceramics and material-culture programme.
notes.openai: A contemporary gallery known for introducing Korean and wider Asian artists to Hong Kong audiences.

notes.anthropic: Independent, artist-led space in Sham Shui Po known for discursive programmes, sound events and support of very young practitioners.
notes.openai: An artist-led experimental platform valued for collaborative, process-based and alternative exhibition formats.

notes.anthropic: International chain gallery with a long-standing Hong Kong presence selling modern masters alongside blue-chip contemporary names.
notes.openai: A globally networked gallery with strong secondary-market and established contemporary holdings.

notes.anthropic: Unusual programme connecting Central and Eastern European artists with Asian audiences through curated, research-led exhibitions.
notes.openai: A young international gallery mounting focused presentations by emerging and mid-career artists.

notes.anthropic: Dedicated photography gallery documenting Hong Kong's urban identity, representing Fan Ho's estate and a new generation of local photographers.
notes.openai: An important specialist in Hong Kong photography, including both historical masters and contemporary image-makers.

notes.anthropic: Hotel-hosted non-commercial space that gave many emerging Hong Kong artists and curators early exhibition opportunities.
notes.openai: A socially engaged contemporary space whose exhibitions frequently address identity, community and regional politics.

notes.anthropic: Heritage tong lau converted into a multi-floor art space with a curated, community-minded programme of local and international shows.
notes.openai: An architecturally distinctive project space hosting tightly curated exhibitions by local and international artists.

galleries.name: Mizuma Gallery
galleries.address_hint: K11 ATELIER King's Road, 728 King's Road

notes.openai: The Hong Kong presence of an important Japanese gallery known for distinctive Asian contemporary practices.

notes.anthropic: Long-running gallery with a distinctive focus on Indonesian and Southeast Asian contemporary artists.
notes.openai: A longstanding gallery with a personal, cross-cultural programme centered on Southeast Asian and diasporic artists.

notes.anthropic: Tokyo gallery known for Yayoi Kusama and Southeast Asian artists such as Tang Da Wu and Chim↑Pom; a key Japanese presence in Hong Kong.

galleries.name: f22 foto space
galleries.address_hint: Amber Commercial Building, 70 Morrison Hill Road

notes.anthropic: Photography-dedicated space presenting international masters and Hong Kong photographers with well-produced exhibitions and books.
notes.openai: A specialist photography venue with exhibitions, publications and strong links to the regional photographic community.

notes.anthropic: French-founded photography gallery on Hollywood Road, a consistent venue for documentary and fine-art photography in the city.
notes.openai: A dedicated photography gallery presenting established international and Asian artists.

notes.anthropic: Tokyo-rooted gallery popular for contemporary pop, urban and figurative artists with a strong young collector following.
notes.openai: A Hong Kong-founded gallery with an international footprint and a popular programme of emerging contemporary art.
A nonprofit studio and exhibition platform fostering emerging Hong Kong artists and cross-disciplinary exchange.

galleries.name: Alisan Fine Arts
galleries.address_hint: Hing Wai Centre, 7 Tin Wan Praya Road

notes.anthropic: Founded 1981 by Alice King; the pioneering dealer of the New Ink movement and Chinese-diaspora modernists, with a second Central space.

notes.openai: A Hong Kong-founded platform producing site-responsive exhibitions and cross-border projects with contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Multi-floor gallery driving the street-art-adjacent and figurative contemporary market in Asia, with a young international collector base.

galleries.name: ArtisTree
galleries.address_hint: Cambridge House, Taikoo Place, 979 King's Road

notes.openai: A substantial corporate-supported venue for contemporary art, performance and cross-disciplinary cultural programming.

galleries.name: Floating Projects
galleries.address_hint: 8/F Sing Teck Factory Building, 44 Wong Chuk Hang Road

notes.anthropic: Artist-run collective space founded by Linda Lai; a laboratory for experimental media, sound and research-based practice.
notes.openai: An artist-run platform with a sustained commitment to experimentation, collaboration and alternative forms of display.
An international gallery emphasizing cross-cultural abstraction, photography and artists from across Asia.

notes.anthropic: Non-profit photography centre running exhibitions, courses and publications that sustain Hong Kong's photographic community.
notes.openai: A longstanding nonprofit photography organization combining exhibitions, education and support for local practitioners.

notes.anthropic: Boutique gallery in the Wong Chuk Hang cluster with an abstraction-leaning programme of Asian and European artists.
notes.openai: A regional contemporary gallery known for approachable exhibitions by Asian emerging and mid-career artists.
A locally established gallery with a broad programme spanning Asian contemporary art and emerging practices.

names.anthropic: CHAT (Centre for Heritage, Arts and Textile)

notes.openai: An energetic younger gallery cultivating Hong Kong talent and accessible entry points into contemporary collecting.
A critically minded emerging gallery presenting conceptually focused solo and group exhibitions.

notes.openai: A focused photography gallery supporting experimental and artist-led approaches to the medium.

notes.anthropic: Hong Kong joint venture with Tokyo's NANZUKA, showing Japanese pop, manga-influenced and design-adjacent contemporary artists.

notes.openai: An independent cultural space supporting socially engaged exhibitions, publications and grassroots art activity.
A distinctive gallery introducing Italian radical art, design and postwar visual culture to Hong Kong.
A commercial gallery presenting Chinese and international artists with an emphasis on material and nature-based practices.
A Shanghai- and Hong Kong-connected gallery supporting emerging and mid-career Chinese contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Emerging-artist gallery known for conceptually driven solo presentations by young Chinese and international artists.

notes.openai: A locally based gallery presenting contemporary painting and mixed-media work by Asian and international artists.
A contemporary gallery particularly visible for sculpture, ceramics and materially driven Asian practices.
An intimate neighborhood gallery with a history of supporting independent artists and locally engaged projects.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run space by Clara Cheung and Gum Cheng, long a platform for socially and politically engaged Hong Kong art and art education.

notes.openai: A flexible gallery and event venue that gives independent artists and curators a visible public platform.

notes.openai: A Hong Kong gallery presenting contemporary painting, sculpture and cross-cultural group exhibitions.

notes.openai: An established independent gallery emphasizing affordable contemporary work and emerging international artists.
A socially conscious photography gallery focused on Hong Kong street life, local narratives and accessible collecting.
A compact neighborhood venue offering regular exposure to local and regional contemporary artists.
A specialist platform elevating contemporary ceramics and craft-based practices within a fine-art context.
A younger Central gallery presenting emerging artists from Hong Kong, Asia and the international market.

notes.anthropic: Independent Kowloon space focused on photography, publishing and cross-disciplinary projects by younger practitioners.

notes.openai: An emerging gallery noted for intimate, experimental presentations and a younger international roster.

notes.anthropic: Design- and publishing-oriented space whose exhibitions and talks helped make Tai Nan Street a creative district.

notes.openai: An independent artist-led room contributing to Hong Kong's small-scale experimental exhibition ecology.

notes.openai: A photography-focused platform supporting exhibitions, publications and wider public engagement with the medium.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run industrial-building space supporting experimental installation and performance outside the commercial districts.

notes.openai: The Asian space of a European gallery recognized for media art, photography and technology-conscious practices.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run space in a Kowloon East factory building known for raw, low-budget experimental exhibitions and gatherings.

notes.openai: A Hong Kong gallery promoting contemporary Chinese artists through exhibitions and collector-oriented research.

notes.anthropic: Sound-art organisation running residencies, listening projects and exhibitions that have shaped Hong Kong's sonic art discourse.

notes.openai: A visible platform for pop-influenced, urban and emerging art with strong engagement among younger collectors.

notes.anthropic: Art-education non-profit connecting Hong Kong with Southeast and East Asian artists through exchange programmes and exhibitions.
